reviews.text:
A very nice app!. Simple to set up, easy to use.
Some fiddling with the calibration is necessary, but within three days, I am satisfied with the accuracy.
Then again, I'm concerned with 'more steps than yesterday', so a 'ballpark' figure is fine for me.
Recommend this highly!
Awesome!. Great App.
Dawn. Works like champ!

Inaccurate counter. Carefully counting steps, I find that this pedometer app is usually off by 200%. It works fine if you walk steadily on a hard road surface and then shut down the app, but if you keep your iPhone with you throughout the day with the app running can be off by thousands of steps. Frequently you get steps by texting. Riding in a car will give you a few steps every time the car hits a tiny bump. You have to open the app and turn it on at the start of a walk, then reopen the app and turn it off at the end of your walk if you want to count steps or estimate miles travelled.
Lots of nice features and easy to use but no real support. "Detection of a Walk" function sounds nice but doesn't appear to work.
The sensitivity is easily set but mysteriously labelled - does "Stronger" mean more sensitive to motion or less sensitive to motion?
One nice feature is that you can turn off the GPS function to save battery power.

Very handy. This app is so easy to use I love it. My only complaint is the map is inaccurate. I would like to keep track of my route as I often walk in the woods however it isn't even close. Other than that I love it.

Works for walk in place. I just tested it with walk in place side to side and marching up and down, and unlike others I've tried - it counts everything while I'm doing something else on the phone (reading, playing games, watching tv, etc.) so this is the first iPhone pedometer that I can use since that's my major activity. It also counted steps in my pocket (loose overalls). I set it on highest sensitivity and it may be overestimating steps, but it still gives me an idea of my activity level for the day. It doesn't count "chair walking" however (walk in place movements while sitting down), so if I want to count that I'll just track time. But I'm quite happy with it. Nice that the badge shows the steps so you don't have to open it. I'm putting it on the first page...
